subject: Operational uplift and capacity agreement for H2 launch
messages:
From: Sarah Chen <sarah@cloudfax.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-09-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity needs and support for Sept product launch

Hi Marcus,

Quick note from CloudFax — we're ramping up for our September product push and expect peak inference volume to increase ~3x for two weeks post-launch. We want to discuss tightening our SLAs and moving to a higher support tier at renewal (term ends 2028-09-30).

Key asks: 
- 95th pctl latency target (currently 420ms) — can you get this down to ~300–350ms with a dedicated pool?
- Priority respond window for incidents during launch week
- Temporary burst capacity and assurance on autoscale behavior

I've attached our internal usage summary for July–Aug for context (CloudFax_MVP_usage_report.pdf). Can we sync this week? Looping procurement shortly.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Chen
Head of Platform
CloudFax

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah@cloudfax.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-09-07T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity needs and support for Sept product launch

Hi Sarah — thanks for the context and the attachment, very helpful. Short answer: we can design a short-term uplift and a permanent SLA elevation at renewal that meets your needs. Proposed approach: 

1) Pilot uplift window (launch week): reserved dedicated pool sized for +3x expected peak, with automated burst credits to absorb spikes; no throttling under the reserved quota.
2) Premium SLA at renewal: 99.95% availability and a 95th percentile latency SLO configurable by workload. For your profile we can target 350ms on the dedicated pool; 300ms is aggressive but we can discuss optimizations (quantization/sequence bucketing).
3) Incident response: priority P1/P2 routing to a named on-call, 30-minute initial response for P1 during the launch window.
4) Pricing: uplift in committed spend for the dedicated pool + one-time onboarding and runbook work. I'll loop ops for precise numbers.

I've attached a draft term sheet (Redwood_SLA_Termsheet_v1.docx) with the high-level options. Can we do a 30-min call tomorrow to walk the options and surface procurement constraints? I'll bring Evelyn for ops and Lauren for commercial terms. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/DF-34820-U2

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Director, Account Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Termsheet_v1.docx

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah@cloudfax.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.inference>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-09-07T12:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity needs and support for Sept product launch

Hi Sarah — quick ops note from my side after reviewing your usage file. A few operational commitments we can make for the launch: 

- Autoscale and warm pool: we'll pre-warm a dedicated pool in us-west for the 10-day launch window; that reduces cold-start variance and helps latency.
- KV/prefix caching: if you can provide common prompt sets we'll configure prefix caching to lower per-token work.
- Burst credits: we can set a burst pool equivalent to 30% of your committed TPS for emergency traffic; costs are applied to the committed plan at a discounted overage rate.
- Runbook & handoff: 2-hour on-call knowledge transfer + a tailored runbook for your SREs.

Operational constraints to confirm: final model family (affects kernel selection and latency), average sequence length, and whether any traffic will come from EU/APAC regions during the launch (affects placement).

I added suggested SLO numbers in the attached term sheet and a short ops checklist. Happy to review on a call.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Termsheet_v1.docx

From: Sarah Chen <sarah@cloudfax.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.inference>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@cloudfax.com
Date: 2028-09-08T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity needs and support for Sept product launch

Thanks Marcus and Evelyn — this is a helpful start. A couple of asks from our side after internal review: 

- Can you aim for a 95th pctl latency of 300ms rather than 350ms? We understand there may be a premium for that.
- For procurement: we prefer a 12-month committed term with a 30% reserve uplift for launch-week, then scale down.
- Pilot pricing: would you be open to a reduced rate for the initial two-week uplift to validate behavior?

We're available for a call Thursday morning PT. Procurement is looped in on cc; they will want the updated term sheet and a DocuSign-ready SLA.

Best,
Sarah

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah@cloudfax.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference>, procurement@cloudfax.com
Date: 2028-09-09T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity needs and support for Sept product launch — next steps and updated term sheet

Sarah — thanks, we discussed internally and can accommodate your asks with the following commitments: 

- Target 95th pctl latency: we'll target 320ms baseline on the dedicated pool with an optimization plan to hit 300ms depending on model choice and prompt shaping. We'll include two opt windows in the first 30 days to tune quantization and batching.
- 12-month committed term with a one-time launch-week 30% reserved uplift and discounted pilot price for the two-week uplift (50% off uplift overage).
- Incident SLA: named on-call and 30-minute P1 response during launch week; post-launch standard priority windows apply.

Attached is the updated term sheet (Redwood_SLA_Termsheet_v2.docx). If that looks good, I'll send a DocuSign link for signature and book a kickoff workshop with Ops. DocuSign preview: https://docusign.com/xyz/CloudFax-SLA-v2

Proposed next steps: 
- You and procurement review the draft SLA (attached)
- Sign via DocuSign by 2028-09-15 to secure pre-warm window
- Kickoff workshop week of 2028-09-18

Meeting invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abc123

Thanks — we appreciate the partnership.

Marcus Lin
Director, Account Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Termsheet_v2.docx
